text:
alex: Heads-up — deployed QuietScheduler v0.9 to canary yesterday evening. Initial numbers look solid: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 down ~9%, p99 down ~18% on small-sequence traffic. Cost per token reduced ~11% on the canary fleet.

maria: whoa nice. what's the main change?

alex: two small but compounding changes: 1) jitter-smoothing window that prevents microbursts from creating tiny single-request batches; 2) drain-time adaptive packing — lets the packer hold a tiny grace window (~10ms) if it expects more tokens for the same request, which increases batch hit rate for multi-chunk inputs.

samir: any tradeoffs? extra latency for individual requests?

alex: measured tail tradeoffs are positive — p50 stable, p95 improved, only a ~1-2ms bump for very short single-chunk requests, which is net win because batching reduces queuing spikes elsewhere.

lia: curious about long-seq behavior — does the grace window cause extra KV churn?
alex: good question. we added a short-circuit: if seq_len > 1024 or model is streaming-heavy, grace window is bypassed. also prefetch KV warmups triggered on pattern detect so churn is minimal.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: QuietScheduler v0.9 -> canary cluster (canary-17) SUCCESS at 2024-09-18T22:12:14Z

maria: can we get the config snippet for ops?

alex: pasted below: 

```
pack_policy: adaptive
jitter_smooth_ms: 6
grace_window_ms: 10
seq_len_bypass_threshold: 1024
enable_prefetch_pattern: true
```

samir: where are the bench dashboards?
alex: dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/quiet-scheduler/canary-17 (perf vs baseline, cost delta, error rates). summary numbers in the dashboard note: token cost -11.2%, p99 latency -18.4% for small-seq traffic (sampled from search and chat-lite routes).

lia: any anomalous errors during canary?
alex: none beyond the usual transient 429s during yesterday's load spike. We throttled canary traffic down and re-ran; stable since.

maria: timeline for wider rollout?
alex: plan: small regional flip this week — 10% of eu-west clusters, observe 48h; if green, progressively 25% -> 50% next week. will add automated rollback if p99 regresses by >5% or error rate >0.5%.

samir: can we get a quick RFC/one-pager for the console release notes and marketing bullets?
alex: sure — I'll drop a short blurb in #announcements and attach to the release notes. draft: "QuietScheduler: microburst smoothing and adaptive drain packing reduce p99 latency up to ~18% and lower token cost by ~11% for small-sequence workloads."

lia: can SRE add a synthetic job that hits edge cases (long seq + burst) so we don't surprise customers?

alex: yes, created a job: perf-synth/quiet-scheduler-edge (runs every 2h).

deploy-bot: Canary -> eu-west-1 flip (10%) scheduled by alex for 2024-09-20T03:00:00Z

maria: nice work team :tada:

samir: can we log the packer metrics to the trace span so we can correlate in Sentry? small PR?

alex: opened PR #4123 to add span attrs: pack_size, grace_wait_ms, bypass_flag. landing today.

maria: any quick followups for product? does this change recommended defaults for new customers?

alex: not yet. keep defaults conservative for Private customers. For Hosted we'll expose an opt-in toggle in Console labeled "Adaptive packing (QuietScheduler)" and recommend it for chat/search workloads.

lia: thumbs up. let's watch cost dashboards closely.

alex: will post a final canary wrap with numbers after 48h of eu-west run. thanks for the quick reviews.
